title: S018 — Node-set & topology-aware frontier soundness
description: Determine whether the S017 false negatives can be eliminated by explicitly modeling node-set and topology changes, from a principled finite set of pre-propagation state variables, without creating a second semantic engine.
result_summary: HOLD. Adding pre-propagation node-set + edge-endpoint + cycle-membership terms to the S017 frontier ELIMINATES the false negatives (FN 3 -> 0): the frontier is SOUND on both canons for all seven operations. The S017 edge residue is fully explained by node-set change + edge-endpoint change. BUT the sound frontier is GLOBAL: F18 is approximately the whole model (verrin 14/14, ordos 18/18) with precision about 1 percent (FP 6339), because cycle membership - the one input that removes the last false negatives - is globally connected through the same reverse index. Fallback frequency is about 100 percent, so a local->global hybrid buys no locality. Shadow-engine audit: all inputs are class A (structural) or B (existing semantic state); the frontier only over-approximates WHICH nodes might change, never a judgment value; no class D. Semantic authority remains singular. Conclusion: locality can be predicted soundly without a second engine, but only at global scope.

answers.Q3_smallest_sufficient_state: previous + current node sets, edge endpoints, cycle membership, reverse dependency index
answers.Q4_structural_or_semantic: structural (class A/B only); no propagation semantics reconstructed
answers.Q5_remaining_global_triggers: cycle membership (the globaliser) and node-set changes
answers.Q6_isolatable_fallback: yes but it fires ~100% of the time on these canons, so it buys no locality
answers.Q8_one_or_two_engines: ONE engine - the predictive layer only over-approximates which nodes might change

next_experiment: reconsider the execution architecture around a different boundary: seeding Phase A from a prior truth (a semantic-execution change, out of S018 scope) rather than elaborating invalidation rules.
limitations: Seed canons + 200-step random histories only; the 21-topology adversarial corpus was not built (budget).
Precision (~1%) reported, not optimised (the brief forbids optimising).
